@graph.description: A practical AI agent task management workflow for agents that claim work, post updates, report results, and close tasks through CLI and MCP.

itemListElement.name: AI Agent Task Management: The Claim, Update, Report, Close Loop

mainEntity.name: What is AI agent task management?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI agent task management is the workflow for letting AI agents operate real tasks on a shared board. The agent reads the task, claims it, posts progress, reports the result, and moves it to the next state. The goal is not just task generation. The goal is a reliable lifecycle where humans can see what agents are doing and review their output asynchronously.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from AI project management?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI project management is the broader system: planning, boards, workflows, agent access, attribution, reporting, and human approval. AI agent task management is the narrower execution loop inside that system. It focuses on how an individual agent handles one task from claim to close. For the broader guide, read AI agents in project management.

mainEntity.name: Should agents use CLI or MCP to update tasks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use MCP when the agent is working inside an interactive AI environment such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf. Use the CLI when the agent is running as a script, cron job, CI step, or autonomous loop. Both can support the same lifecycle. The choice is about the agent runtime, not about which one is universally better.

mainEntity.name: Should AI agents be allowed to close tasks themselves?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes. For low-risk tasks with deterministic validation, direct close can be fine. For code, customer-facing copy, pricing, production changes, data changes, or anything ambiguous, the safer default is for agents to move work to Review and let a human close it. Define this by task type so the rule is predictable.

mainEntity.name: How do you keep agent updates from becoming notification overload?

acceptedAnswer.text: Anchor every update to the task and route only attention-worthy items to the inbox. Claim comments and routine status notes can be low-noise. Blockers, review requests, and human mentions should surface clearly. The inbox should help humans batch-review agent work instead of forcing them to watch agent sessions live.
